messages.text:
"Implement the solution in src/main/java/BankAccount.java, src/main/java/BankAccountActionInvalidException.java so that the tests in src/test/java/BankAccountTest.java pass. The specification follows.

# Instructions

Your task is to implement bank accounts supporting opening/closing, withdrawals, and deposits of money.

As bank accounts can be accessed in many different ways (internet, mobile phones, automatic charges), your bank software must allow accounts to be safely accessed from multiple threads/processes (terminology depends on your programming language) in parallel.
For example, there may be many deposits and withdrawals occurring in parallel; you need to ensure there are no [race conditions][wikipedia] between when you read the account balance and set the new balance.

It should be possible to close an account; operations against a closed account must fail.

[wikipedia]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_condition#In_software


# Instructions append

This exercise introduces [concurrency][oracle-docs-concurrency].
To pass the last test you might find the [`synchronized` keyword or locks][oracle-docs-synchronized] useful.

Problems arising from running code concurrently are often intermittent because they depend on the order the code is executed.
Therefore the last test runs many [threads][threads-api] several times to increase the chances of catching a bug.
That means this test should fail if your implementation is not [thread safe][wiki-thread-safety], but there is a chance it will pass just because there was no concurrent modification attempt.
It is unlikely that this will occur several times in a row since the order the code is executed should vary every time you run the test.
So if you run the last test a couple of times and it passes every time then you can be reasonably sure that your implementation is correct.

[oracle-docs-concurrency]: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/essential/concurrency/index.html
[oracle-docs-synchronized]: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/essential/concurrency/locksync.html
[threads-api]: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Thread.html
[wiki-thread-safety]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thread_safety


Do NOT modify the tests or the build files except as stated below. Do not create new files unless the specification requires them; Helper classes may go only in the solution's package."

The file already exists in src/main/java. Let's try reading it.

The exception class is already fine. Implement BankAccount. Note: withdraw's negative check — the test withdraws -50 with a balance of 100 and expects "Cannot deposit or withdraw negative amount". Also, the test withdraws 50 with a balance of 25 and expects "Cannot withdraw more money than is currently in the account". Order of checks: the negative check should come first (withdrawal of -50 with balance 100: if the balance check came first, -50 <= 100 would pass and the wrong message would be returned). Therefore, check amount < 0 first.
The exception class is already complete. Now I'll implement `BankAccount`:

Note: the test expects "Account closed" for a deposit into an account that hasn't been opened (isOpen=false → "Account closed" — correct). close on an account that hasn't been opened → "Account not open". Good.

Run the tests.
No output, quiet mode, exit code 0 — tests passed. Just to be safe, I'll run the concurrency tests a few more times.

content.text: All 3 runs passed, including the concurrency tests. Done.

All tests pass. I implemented the solution in `src/main/java/BankAccount.java`:

- **State**: a `boolean isOpen` flag and an `int balance`, both guarded by the object's intrinsic lock — every method (`open`, `close`, `getBalance`, `deposit`, `withdraw`) is `synchronized`, so the read-modify-write cycles (e.g., `balance -= amount`) are atomic and the 1000-thread concurrency test is safe.
- **`open()`**: throws `"Account already open"` if open; otherwise sets the account open and resets the balance to 0 (so a reopened account starts empty).
- **`close()`**: throws `"Account not open"` if not open; otherwise closes and zeroes the balance.
- **`getBalance()` / `deposit()` / `withdraw()`**: throw `"Account closed"` when the account isn't open (covers both closed and never-opened accounts); `deposit` rejects negative amounts, and `withdraw` rejects negative amounts *before* the overdraft check (so `withdraw(-50)` reports the negative-amount error even when funds exist), then rejects withdrawals exceeding the balance with `"Cannot withdraw more money than is currently in the account"`.

`BankAccountActionInvalidException.java` already had the required constructor, so it needed no changes. I ran the full test suite four times (including `--rerun-tasks` to force the concurrency test to re-execute) and it passed every run.
